content.thinking:
I need to avoid including any actual numbers in the postmortem, using placeholders like {alert_raised} and {duration} instead of figures, and keep timeline labels generic. Since there are no pre-existing action items, I'll start numbering mine as AI-1, AI-2, and reference them by that numbering in the contributing factors section.

Tracing the causal chain: the HighErrorRate alert fired, then Argus couldn't determine the cause because metrics for that window came back empty with no explanation given, flag history showed no recent changes, and the issue was escalated — so I should state honestly that the root cause was never determined since the investigation stopped where the evidence ran out. For contributing factors, I'll note the empty metrics retrieval with no fallback sources and the investigator closing out too quickly; action items should include investigating the empty metrics issue, adding fallback data sources, alerting on empty reads, and escalating to a human on-call. I also need to avoid count words like "one candidate" and instead phrase it as "the only candidate" to stay figure-free, and use the {duration} placeholder in the executive summary to express the lower-bound outage time.

action_items.item: Find out why the per-minute metrics read for io-shop returned no data for the incident window. Check the metrics store, the query anchoring on the alert minute and whether the service was reporting at all. Record the finding.

Give the Investigator fallback evidence sources for when metrics are missing: application logs, recent deploys and config changes, and upstream or dependency health. It should try these before it concludes there is insufficient evidence.
Alert when the metrics read for an alerting service returns empty or is stale. A telemetry gap would then show up as its own problem instead of as an unexplained escalation.
Change the escalation handoff so it lists what was checked, what came back empty, and which first manual checks to run. It should also state plainly that the impact figures are unmeasured.

causal_chain.step: Users of io-shop hit errors. The HighErrorRate alert fired at {alert_raised}. That time is the only onset available, because no earlier onset could be measured. The service had not recovered by the last minute of metrics read.

Argus could not say why the errors were happening. The Investigator asked for the service's per-minute metrics around the alert and got nothing back, so it had no error-rate or timing data to reason from.
With no data, the Investigator produced only a placeholder candidate: no cause determined because no metrics were retrieved. It gave that candidate no confidence and tested it with no action.

The only other source checked was the flag provider's history, which showed no recent flag changes. That ruled out a flag change as the trigger but pointed to no alternative. Argus escalated the incident for insufficient evidence. The record does not show why the metrics read was empty, so the chain stops here.

contributing_factors.factor: The investigation relied on one data source. When the metrics read came back empty, no fallback such as logs, recent deploys or dependency health was used, and the incident escalated within moments with nothing learned.

An empty metrics result was not treated as a fault in its own right. The record does not show whether the metrics store, the query anchoring or the service's reporting failed, so the cause of the missing data is unknown.
The escalation carried no useful findings and no guidance for the person receiving it. The handoff said only that evidence was insufficient.

input.executive_summary: An automated alert reported that the io-shop service was returning too many errors. The alert fired at {alert_raised}. The service had not recovered by the last metrics available, so it was broken for at least {duration}. That is a lower bound, not a measured outage length. The error rate and the number of affected users are unknown because the incident's metrics could not be read. Argus's automated response lasted {held} and closed at {closed}. The investigation found no metrics for the incident window and no recent feature-flag changes. It could not name a cause, tried no fix, and escalated to people with the status "insufficient evidence". The fault was still unexplained when the response ended.

went_well: The alert was received and picked up at once, and the incident moved through its states without delay.
Argus did not guess a cause or take a risky action on no evidence. It checked flag history and escalated honestly.
went_wrong: The metrics for the incident window could not be read, so the error rate, onset and impact are all unknown.
Argus escalated without a cause, any mitigation, or any finding beyond the absence of recent flag changes.
The only candidate cause was a placeholder, so the incident ended without any account of why users saw errors.

input.root_cause: The cause of the io-shop errors was not determined. The Investigator's request for per-minute metrics returned nothing, and the flag history showed no recent changes. Argus had no evidence to work from and escalated. The record does not say why the metrics read came back empty.
